name: Spackle
description: A gray paste synthesized from scraped SNT-coating residue harvested off junked neural interface cards, suspended in industrial glycerin and cut with veterinary-grade lidocaine. Applied directly to exposed chrome ports or BCI contact pads, it temporarily supercharges signal throughput between organic tissue and augmentation hardware. Extremely popular with runners who need their chrome performing above rated specs for a few hours.
effects: augmentation performance boost 40-80% above rated specs
heightened proprioceptive awareness of chrome limbs
mild euphoria from nervous system stimulation
side_effects: uncontrolled muscle spasms in augmented limbs
interface rejection cascade if paste contacts corrupted hardware
rare: permanent nerve deadening around port
cultural_context: Spackle is the Shelf worker's performance enhancer — used by dockworkers, salvage crews, and unlicensed couriers who run chrome that's two generations old and held together with zip ties. Using it is seen as a mark of desperation or respect depending on context. Old heads say you can tell a Spackle veteran by the gray ring scars around their ports.
story_hooks: A courier running a critical package discovers their Spackle batch was cut with something that's causing their arm to seize mid-run — they need to complete the job anyway
A Shelf chemist has figured out how to synthesize clean SNT-coating without scrapping hardware, potentially disrupting both the junk market and legitimate augmentation supply chains
Someone is deliberately contaminating Spackle batches in the Calumet District — three runners have had interface rejection cascades in one week
